lines.en: Okay, here’s my practice. **Today I’m going to talk about** recycling at school.
lines.pt: Certo, aqui está meu ensaio. Hoje vou falar sobre reciclagem na escola.

lines.en: Nice start. Say your name first, then the topic, and smile.
lines.pt: Bom começo. Diga seu nome primeiro, depois o tema, e sorria.

lines.en: Got it. **First,** I’ll explain why plastic is a problem. **Then** I’ll show three easy solutions.
lines.pt: Entendi. Primeiro, vou explicar por que o plástico é um problema. Depois mostro três soluções fáceis.

lines.en: Good. Add an example, so people remember your idea.
lines.pt: Bom. Acrescente um exemplo, para as pessoas lembrarem da sua ideia.

lines.en: Right. **For example,** our cafeteria uses a lot of plastic bottles every day.
lines.pt: Certo. Por exemplo, nossa lanchonete usa muitas garrafas plásticas todos os dias.

lines.en: That works. How will you finish your talk?
lines.pt: Isso funciona. Como você vai terminar a apresentação?

lines.en: **To sum up,** small changes make a big difference. **Thank you for listening.**
lines.pt: Resumindo, pequenas mudanças fazem uma grande diferença. Obrigada por ouvirem.

lines.en: Perfect. Slow down a little, and ask if there are any questions.
lines.pt: Perfeito. Fale um pouco mais devagar e pergunte se há dúvidas.

pages.title: A Short Presentation

situation.text: You must give a short presentation in class. You practice with a classmate: open the talk, explain your points in order, give an example and finish clearly.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can give a two-minute talk with an opening, two or three ordered points, an example and a closing, and answer a question.
canDo: Open a talk: Today I’m going to talk about…
Order your ideas: First… Then… Finally…
Close the talk: To sum up… Thank you for listening.
pages.think: Do you feel nervous when you speak in front of people? What helps you feel calm?

teach.goal: Abrir a aula pela situação real: uma apresentação curta com começo, meio e fim.
solo: Leia o objetivo em voz alta e peça que o estudante diga com as próprias palavras o que vai fazer hoje.
Pergunte “Think about it” antes de mostrar qualquer expressão.
group: Cada estudante diz um tema sobre o qual poderia falar por dois minutos.
Mostre os 4 critérios de sucesso: é a missão final da aula.
extra: Have you ever given a presentation in English?
What topic could you talk about for two minutes?
support: Aceite respostas curtas ou em português na primeira rodada e reformule em inglês.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Start with real questions about the student’s life, then link them to today’s situation.
intro.group: One question per student, then ask a classmate the same question back.

pages.recall: Review: requests at work with Could you…? Ask: Could you explain your job or studies in two sentences?

qs.q: What is something you know a lot about?
qs.pt: Sobre o que você sabe muito?

qs.q: Did you ever speak in front of a group?
qs.pt: Você já falou na frente de um grupo?

qs.q: What makes a talk interesting for you?
qs.pt: O que torna uma apresentação interessante para você?

pages.tip: Use the answers to find gaps and to recycle earlier A2 content. Aim for longer answers: two or three connected sentences.

teach.goal: Entrar no idioma e ativar vocabulário de tópicos pessoais e experiências passadas.
extra: What was the best talk you ever heard?
What do you do before an important talk?
support: Ofereça as respostas-modelo (chips) e peça apenas que escolham uma.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Presentation structure
pages.intro: Many English-speaking audiences like a clear structure. Look and guess before you read.

cards.note: A common structure: say the topic, give your points, then sum up.
“First,” “then” and “finally” help listeners follow your talk.
Speakers usually look at the audience and invite questions at the end.

qs.q: How do speakers usually organize a short talk?
qs.pt: Como se costuma organizar uma apresentação curta?

levels.A2: They open, give two or three points and finish with a summary.
levels.B1: A typical talk has an introduction, a few clear points with examples and a short conclusion.
levels.B2: A clear opening, a logical sequence of points supported by examples and a concise conclusion are the usual expectation.

levels.A2: They help the audience follow the order of ideas.
levels.B1: These words show the audience where you are in the talk.
levels.B2: Signposting guides listeners through the structure so they do not get lost.

qs.q: What do people often do at the end of a talk?
qs.pt: O que as pessoas costumam fazer no final de uma apresentação?

levels.A2: They say thank you and ask if there are any questions.
levels.B1: They thank the audience and invite questions.
levels.B2: They sum up the key idea, thank the audience and open the floor to questions.

pages.compare: In Brazil, some talks start with a long background before the main point. Many English-speaking audiences like to hear the topic early: “Today I’m going to talk about…”. How do you start a talk where you live?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural: estrutura clara e palavras de organização.
solo: Mostre os 3 cartões e peça hipóteses antes de explicar.
Peça que o estudante compare com apresentações que já fez na escola ou no trabalho.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica em uma frase.
Pergunte “Do you agree?” entre colegas.
answers: Q2: ajudam a plateia a seguir a ordem.
Q3: agradecer e perguntar se há dúvidas.
extra: Do you prefer short or long talks?
What do you do when you forget a word?
support: Use as respostas do nível A1 como andaime e peça que repitam.
stretch: B2: explique como adaptar a mesma apresentação para colegas e para um chefe.

pass1.pt: O que a Mina está fazendo?

teach.goal: Compreender a situação antes de ver o texto: ideia principal e depois 5 informações.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: só a ideia principal.
2ª escuta: tema, problema, número de soluções, exemplo e último conselho.
Mostre o texto só depois da 2ª escuta.
group: Escuta coletiva; duplas anotam as respostas antes de revelar.
Compare as respostas entre as duplas e só então mostre o texto.
answers: Pass 2: recycling · plastic · three · cafeteria · slow down.
extra: What advice does Ryo give?
Is Mina’s talk clear? Why?
support: Pause depois de cada fala se necessário.

qs.q: What does Ryo tell her to do first?
opts: Say her name and the topic

qs.q: Why does Ryo want an example?
How does Mina finish the talk?

retell.prompt: Retell the conversation in your own words, at your level.

teach.goal: Ler o diálogo, perceber os chunks e recontar.
solo: O estudante lê o papel da Mina; você lê o do Ryo.
Peça que reconte a conversa no nível que conseguir.
group: Leitura em duplas e troca de papéis.
Reconto em cadeia: uma frase por estudante.
answers: Recycling at school · her name and the topic · so people remember · a summary and thanks
extra: What would YOU say in the opening?
What happens if you forget your next point?
support: Mostre a tradução (botão PT) depois da 2ª leitura.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.en: Today I’m going to talk about…
items.use: Open a talk and introduce the topic.
Give an example to explain an idea.

items.en: Today I’m going to talk about sleep.
For example, many people drink coffee late.
To sum up, sleep is important.

pages.note: Choose the four ★ expressions to use again and again. The others help you understand and stretch.

teach.goal: Escolher 4 chunks para uso repetido e descobrir a função de cada um.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?” antes de dar o significado.
Peça que o estudante use cada ★ em uma frase sobre um tema dele.
group: Cada estudante escolhe a expressão que mais usaria e explica quando.
Compare em duplas: onde cada expressão aparece numa apresentação?
answers: Opening · Ordering ideas · Giving an example · Closing · Ordering ideas
extra: Which expression helps you the most when you are nervous?
support: Trabalhe só 3 das expressões ★ na primeira rodada.

errors.r: First, then, finally (mais natural em fala).

patterns.name: Opening a talk
patterns.formula: **Today I’m going to talk about** + noun
ex: Today I’m going to talk about sleep.
Today I’m going to talk about my hometown.
Today I’m going to talk about healthy habits.

patterns.name: Giving an example
ex: For example, our cafeteria uses plastic bottles.
For example, I walk to work every day.

patterns.name: Closing
ex: To sum up, small changes matter.
To sum up, sleep helps us learn.

swap.frame: Today I’m going to talk about {topic}. {order}, I’ll {action}.

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: Today I’m going to talk about sleep.
This presentation will focus on sleep.
The first section describes the problem.
register.note: These are differences of context and register, not absolute rules: “To sum up” is used in both speech and writing.

teach.goal: Fixar 2 padrões principais (01 e 02); os outros são expansão. Usar a troca de palavras para variar a fala.
solo: Mostre o padrão DENTRO do diálogo (grife os chunks).
Use “Swap the words”: toque em cada peça e peça que o estudante diga a frase completa.
Compare spoken × written em 2 exemplos.
group: Troca em cadeia: cada estudante muda UMA peça e o próximo repete a frase.
Em pares: um escolhe as peças, o outro fala.
teach.answers: Padrão 01/02 são o foco; 03/04 são expansão para quem avançar rápido.
extra: Open your own talk with Today I’m going to talk about…
Change one word and say the new sentence.
support: Fique só com abertura + First/Then/Finally na primeira rodada.
stretch: Adicionar uma transição: Now let’s move on to the solutions.

errors.w: Today I talk about my city.
errors.r: Today I’m going to talk about my city.

errors.w: First of all, I will to explain.

errors.r: For example, I like… (vírgula depois de For example)

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: Speakers pause between ideas, not between every word: “Today I’m going to talk about / recycling at school.” Short pauses help the audience follow you. The goal is to be clear and natural, not to remove your accent.

items.say: Today I’m going to talk about recycling.
items.linked: Today I’m gonna talk about | RE-cy-cling.

items.say: To sum up, small changes matter.
items.linked: To SUM UP | SMALL CHAN-ges MAT-ter.

opts: To sum up, | small changes matter.
To sum | up small changes matter.
To sum up small | changes matter.
identify.say: To sum up, small changes matter.

own.prompt: Write your own opening sentence and your first point for a talk.
own.criteria: Say them with a short pause after the opening. Could your partner follow where one idea ended?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: pausas e grupos de ideias (thought groups).
solo: 3 passagens: escutar e identificar → reproduzir ritmo e pausas → usar em abertura e primeiro ponto próprios.
Marque as pausas com uma barra no texto e peça que o estudante respire nelas.
group: Coro, depois duplas; circule ouvindo.
Cada estudante lê um trecho com as pausas marcadas pelo colega.
answers: Identify 1: First, | I’ll explain the problem. · Identify 2: To sum up, | small changes matter.
support: Reduza a velocidade e marque as pausas com barras no texto.

errors.w: Falar tudo sem pausa, muito rápido.
errors.r: Pausar curto depois de cada ideia.

errors.w: Pausar no meio do grupo: To sum | up.

levels.h: Controlled practice — choose the best answer

items.q: 1. You start your talk about healthy habits.
opts: Today I’m going to talk about healthy habits.
items.why: Today I’m going to talk about + topic.

items.q: 2. You want to introduce your second idea.
opts: Then I am show three solution.
items.why: Then + I’ll + verb keeps the order clear.

items.q: 3. You want to explain an idea with a real case.
opts: For example, our cafeteria uses plastic bottles.

items.q: 4. You are at the end of your talk.
opts: To sum up, small changes matter. Thank you for listening.
items.why: To sum up + main idea + thanks.

levels.h: Guided practice — complete, substitute and transform

items.text: Today I’m going to ___ about my city.

ans: Today I’m going to talk about my hometown.
items.model: Today I’m going to talk about my hometown.
items.why: Today I’m going to talk about + topic.

ans: For example, my brother sleeps only five hours.
For example, my brother only sleeps five hours.
For example, my brother sleeps five hours.
items.model: For example, my brother sleeps only five hours.
items.from: Many people sleep too little. / my brother

items.q: You want to ask for time to think. Choose the best reply.
opts: Good question. Let me think for a second.
items.why: A natural way to gain time.

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado: completar, substituir e transformar antes da fala livre.
solo: Peça que o estudante justifique cada resposta.
Se acertar rápido, peça a versão mais informal ou mais formal.
group: Resolvam em duplas e comparem antes de revelar.
Equipes: ponto por resposta justificada.
answers: 1: Today I’m going to talk about healthy habits. · 2: Then I’ll show three solutions. · 3: For example, our cafeteria uses plastic bottles. · 4: To sum up, small changes matter. Thank you for listening.
Gap: talk · Finally · Today I’m going to talk about my hometown. · For example, my brother sleeps only five hours. · Good question. Let me think…
extra: Say each correct answer aloud with pauses.
support: Ofereça o banco de palavras (chips) nas lacunas.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — give a short talk

brief.teacher: You are the audience (ask a question at the end!).
brief.student: You give a one-minute talk about a topic you know well. Open, order, give an example and close.

orders: A talk about a good habit
complications: The audience asks you to repeat a point.
Someone asks a question you don’t understand.
You have only one minute left.

rounds.label: With support
help: Today I’m going to talk about…

teach.goal: Simulação com complicação inesperada e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Combine o tema com um assunto real do aluno (hobby, cidade, trabalho).
Rodada 1: com chunks. Rodada 2: só palavras-chave. Rodada 3: sem roteiro.
Meta de fala: 60–70% do tempo para o estudante. Anote 2–3 correções para a devolutiva.
extra: What if someone asks a question you can’t answer?
support: Volte à rodada 1 se travar; peça que repita só a primeira frase.
stretch: Responda a duas perguntas do público no final.

errors.r: Good question. I’m not sure, but I can find out.

rounds.title: Open the talk
rounds.task: Introduce your topic in two sentences. Your partner gives feedback.
rounds.hint: Today I’m going to talk about…

rounds.title: Order and example
rounds.task: Explain two points in order and give an example.

rounds.title: Close and ask
rounds.task: Close with a summary and invite questions.
rounds.hint: To sum up… Are there any questions?

rounds.title: Share talks
rounds.task: Whole group: each pair shares one talk opening and ending.

infogap.title: Talk planner
infogap.instr: Ask your partner and complete your card. Do not look at the other card!

a.title: You know the topics
a.task: You know two speakers and their topics. Ask about the rest.

b.title: You know the times
b.task: You know the speaking times. Ask about the rest.

teach.goal: Fluência por repetição da função com informações novas a cada rodada.
group: Troque os pares a cada rodada (A+B / C+D → A+C / B+D → A+D / B+C → grupo todo). Com 6 estudantes, três duplas simultâneas.
Sem salas simultâneas: interações sequenciais enquanto uma dupla apresenta.
Responsabilidade individual: cada aluno faz ≥1 pergunta e ≥1 resposta.
answers: Info gap: A tem os temas (Recycling, Sleep); B tem horários (9:30, 2 min; 9:40, 3 min). Cada um completa perguntando.
extra: What is the first speaker’s topic?
How long is the second talk?
support: Entregue frases-modelo no chat da turma.

pages.title: Group mission — a two-minute talk
pages.goal: Each group must prepare and give a short talk in English: open, order the ideas, give an example and close.

missions.mission: Give a talk about a place you love. Include one example and answer a question from the audience.
missions.constraint: Use “Today I’m going to talk about…” and “To sum up…”.
missions.start: Hello everyone! Today I’m going to talk about…

missions.mission: Give a talk about a hobby. The audience must ask two questions.
missions.start: Hi! Today I’m going to talk about…

missions.mission: Give a talk with three tips for learning English. Everyone gives feedback.
missions.constraint: Use a number (three tips) and finish with “Thank you for listening.”
missions.start: Good morning! Today I’m going to give you three tips…

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: o objetivo é comunicar a ideia com clareza.
group: Cada grupo recebe papéis, restrição e missão. Alterne orador e plateia.
Progressão: 1ª rodada com frases de apoio, 2ª só palavras-chave, 3ª sem roteiro.
Observe e anote 2–3 correções prioritárias; devolutiva no fim.
answers: Modelo: “Today I’m going to talk about my hometown. First, I’ll describe it. Then… For example… To sum up… Are there any questions?”
extra: What if the audience doesn’t understand?
support: Dê o início de frase (“Start with”) em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write the opening and closing of a short talk, with three ordered points in the middle.
pages.model: **Today I’m going to talk about** sleep. **First,** I’ll explain why it matters. **Then** I’ll share two simple tips. **For example,** I put my phone away at ten. **To sum up,** good sleep helps us learn. Thank you for listening!
checklist: I closed with To sum up and thanks.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea instead of rewriting everything.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação comunicativa.
solo: Peça o texto; corrija 2–3 pontos prioritários e mostre uma forma mais natural.
group: Cada estudante escreve; depois troquem os textos entre colegas e corrijam em duplas.
extra: Add one question for the audience.
support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

errors.w: First of all, I going to…

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.desc: Mantém a comunicação sem interrupções excessivas.

criteria.name: Language use
criteria.desc: Utiliza adequadamente padrões, vocabulário e expressões.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.desc: É compreensível e usa ritmo e entonação adequados.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Raise complexity and speed; add follow-up questions.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

prompts.well: Example: Your talk had a clear opening, order and ending.
prompts.improve: Example: Pause between ideas, not between every word.
prompts.next: Example: Give a two-minute talk and answer a question without notes.

teach.goal: Avaliar o que o aluno conseguiu comunicar, não só os erros gramaticais. Observe a estrutura (abertura, ordem, fechamento) e o ritmo com pausas.
solo: O estudante se autoavalia primeiro; depois você.
Feche com os três blocos: What you did well · What to improve · Your next challenge.
group: Dê um comentário por critério a cada estudante.
Cada um escolhe o próprio próximo desafio.
teach.answers: A rubrica é uma ferramenta interna de acompanhamento, não uma certificação CEFR.

next: Today I’m going to talk about…

solo: Sem consultar as anotações: abrir uma apresentação, dar um exemplo e fechar.
group: Exit challenge individual; compare com o colega e combine a tarefa de continuidade.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: The structure stays the same; language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: My talk: dogs. Dogs are good.
ladder.goal: Say it with short phrases and models.

ladder.say: Today I’m going to talk about dogs. First, I’ll explain why they are good pets. To sum up, they are loyal.
ladder.goal: Open, order, close with simple phrases.

ladder.say: I’d like to talk about why dogs make good pets. I’ll give three reasons, with a personal example for each one.
ladder.goal: Explain and compare options with connectors.

ladder.say: This afternoon I’d like to explore why dogs are such effective companions, drawing on both research and my own experience.
ladder.goal: Negotiate with nuance and appropriate register.

ladder.say: My aim today is to challenge the assumption that dogs are merely pets, and to argue that they are genuine partners.
I shall argue that the dog’s place in human life is not incidental but constitutive of how we understand loyalty.
ladder.goal: Manage the situation with precision and tact.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
